chunks: And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddhal, who said: I heard Abul Hasan (peace be upon him) say:
Never did two factions meet in combat except that Allah granted victory to the one which was more forgiving.

key_terms.عفو: Forgiveness, pardon, clemency; the act of relinquishing one’s right to retaliate
key_terms.فئتان: Two factions or groups, particularly in the context of armed conflict
key_terms.نصر: Divine victory, help, or support granted by God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about forgiveness and victory in battle?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) articulates a profound principle of divine assistance in conflict: God invariably supports the party that is more inclined toward forgiveness and clemency. This teaching was conveyed to al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddhal, a prominent hadith scholar of the early third century AH. In the socio-political context of frequent sectarian and military conflicts during the Abbasid era, this statement redirected the audience’s focus from military strength to moral superiority as the true determinant of divine support.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 45. And with the first chain of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faddhal, who said: I heard Abul Hassan (i.e. ‘Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha) peace be upon him say: "
Never did the two warring factions meet to fight except that Allah helped the one which is more forgiving."
